title: LINQ — remember
rememberThis: A query variable stores a plan. Each enumeration re-runs it and allocates iterators plus delegate captures.
TryGetNonEnumeratedCount avoids full walk for Count on List/array; ToList snapshots before multiple use.
Query syntax and method syntax compile to the same operators — no performance difference.
IEnumerable uses Func delegates in-process. IQueryable uses expression trees for providers.
PLINQ AsParallel is a measured CPU-bound opt-in on in-memory snapshots — not the default performance answer.
bullets: SelectMany flattens nested sequences; two from clauses are SelectMany.
OrderBy/GroupBy are deferred but buffer the entire source before first yield.
dotMemory shows WhereIterator and Func allocations on hot LINQ chains.
Do not turn IQueryable into an EF Core lecture — know Func vs Expression and the ToList wall.
